founder: Justin Jackson (co-founder, CEO) and Jon Buda (co-founder, President)
founderSource: transistor.fm/about names Jon Buda co-founder/President and Justin Jackson co-founder/CEO; transistor.fm/justin bio: met at XOXO 2014, launched Transistor Aug 2018, documented on Build Your SaaS podcast.
teamSize: 6 people (Jon Buda, Justin Jackson, Helen Ryles, Jason Pearl, Joshua Anderton, Michael Green per transistor.fm/about).
targetCustomer: Indie podcasters, businesses, and networks that want simple hosting with great support.
customerSegment: Indie podcasters, SMBs, networks, and enterprise brands running public or private shows.
coreProblem: Existing podcast hosts were clunky, charged per show, and offered weak analytics and support.
problemFrequency: Weekly: podcasters publish episodes on a recurring schedule and check stats continuously.
problemSeverity: MEDIUM: bad hosting wastes hours and harms listener experience, but free alternatives exist so pain is not existential.
existingAlternatives: Libsyn, Podbean, Buzzsprout, SoundCloud, self-hosted WordPress + PowerPress.
currentUserWorkflow: Creators upload MP3s to a host, copy RSS feed, manually submit to Apple/Spotify, check fragmented stats, pay per show.
productSolution: Simple, reliable podcast hosting with unlimited shows, strong analytics, private podcasting, and human support from a calm indie team.
coreFeature: Unlimited shows per account, IAB-style analytics, private feeds, dynamic ads, built-in websites, API.
initialMVP: Basic podcast hosting: upload episodes, generate RSS, submit to Apple/Spotify, simple analytics; launched Aug 1 2018 after Feb 2018 partnership signing.
featuresNotInMVP: Video hosting, private-podcast subscribers tiers, dynamic ads, AI transcription, analytics API, network websites, MCP server.
currentFeatureSet: Unlimited podcasts/episodes, video hosting, private podcasts, dynamic ads, AI transcription add-on, analytics API, network websites, MCP server.
pricingModel: Tiered subscription by monthly downloads + private-subscriber limits; monthly or yearly (2 months free); transcription as paid add-on.
freeTier: No free tier; all plans start with paid subscription after trial.
trial: 14-day free trial on all plans, no credit card friction stated.
revenueEvidence: Founder-disclosed early MRR ($781 at launch, $4k Dec 2018); current revenue REVENUE NOT PUBLICLY DISCLOSED; team of six serving 30k+ podcasts implies multi-million ARR scale (INFERRED, not stated).
mrrEvidence: REVENUE NOT PUBLICLY DISCLOSED at record level; founder-disclosed: $781 MRR at launch (Jul 23 2018 blog), $4,000+ MRR Dec 2018 (bootstrap-side-project post); both founders full-time from Aug 2019 implying ~$20k+ MRR by then (founder-stated target $21k MRR).
arrEvidence: ARR NOT PUBLICLY DISCLOSED; no founder ARR figure found (only early MRR snapshots).
customerEvidence: 30,000+ podcasts served (about page); 36,000-38,000 podcasters cited on founder page; public customer directory and reviews page.
growthEvidence: $781 MRR at launch (Jul 2018) to $4,000+ MRR by Dec 2018 (founder blog); 20,000 feeds milestone May 2022 (company blog); 30k-38k podcasts 2025-2026 (site pages).
timeToLaunch: ~6 months from partnership signing (Feb 2018) to public launch (Aug 1 2018); Jon had prior hosting code from employer project.
validationMethod: Pre-sold early access: 51 paying customers and $781 MRR before public launch; validated via founder audience demand.
firstUserAcquisition: Justin Jackson's existing audience (blog, books, MegaMaker community) plus Jon's podcast-tool users; Product Hunt launch Aug 1 2018.
first100Users: Justin announced to his MegaMaker/blog audience and X followers; 51 early-access customers pre-launch; launch-week hustle documented on Build Your SaaS eps 22-30.
mainDistribution: Founder audience + Build Your SaaS build-in-public podcast + content/SEO engine.
secondaryDistribution: Affiliates, podcast-ecosystem word of mouth, alternative-comparison SEO pages (/alternative/buzzsprout/ etc.).
seoStrategy: Strong: guides (how to start a podcast), feature pages, competitor-alternative pages, podcast stats pages; organic content engine.
xStrategy: Founder-led X presence (@justinjackson et al.), launch-week hustle, ongoing build-in-public commentary; secondary to podcast/blog.
indieHackersStrategy: Core channel: build-in-public via Build Your SaaS, Justin’s blog essays, MicroConf community ties; audience overlaps IH heavily.
productHuntStrategy: Launched on Product Hunt Aug 1 2018 (linked from about page); no award details public.
hackerNewsStrategy: No documented HN launch strategy; community presence is indie-hacker-adjacent rather than HN-driven.
directOutreach: UNKNOWN: no evidence of cold-outreach motion; sales is self-serve plus enterprise contact form.
partnerships: Podcast Standards Project participation; integrations (Zapier etc.); affiliate program page; no major exclusive partnerships evidenced.
referralViral: Affiliate program (site footer); word-of-mouth via podcaster recommendations; no built-in viral loop evidenced.
techStack: Web app + RSS/analytics pipeline; exact stack NOT PUBLICLY DISCLOSED (founder Rails-background context only; do not assert).
infrastructure: Paid hosting/bandwidth/CDN for audio delivery and websites; exact providers NOT PUBLIC.
aiUsage: AI transcription add-on (paid) and newer AI-adjacent features; core product is hosting/analytics, not AI-led.
devMethod: Bootstrapped build-in-public: weekly Build Your SaaS podcast as co-founder accountability record; calm-company, profit-first pace.

technicalComplexity: MEDIUM: RSS feeds, audio delivery at scale, download-stats deduplication, private-feed auth, directory integrations.
productComplexity: MEDIUM: RSS correctness, directory submissions, stats, private feeds, websites, API.
infraComplexity: MEDIUM: audio CDN/bandwidth costs scale with downloads; RSS + stats pipeline; founders cite infra as core cost.
operationalComplexity: MEDIUM: 6-person team covers support/engineering; audio delivery costs scale with downloads; abuse/moderation load modest.
supportBurden: HIGH at scale: live human chat support is the differentiator and required hiring dedicated success staff (Helen Ryles, Michael Green).
salesComplexity: LOW: pure self-serve signup; enterprise tier adds contact sales but motion is product-led.
differentiation: Unlimited podcasts on every plan, human live-chat support, founder-led transparency, open-podcasting advocacy over walled gardens.
competitiveMoat: Founder brand + build-in-public trust, calm-company support reputation, open-standards advocacy (Podcast Standards Project).
competitors: Buzzsprout, Libsyn, Podbean, Captivate, Castos, Simplecast, Spotify for Creators.
competitiveWeaknesses: Higher starting price than free hosts; no free tier; crowded market with Spotify/YouTube bundling hosting free.
retention: Likely HIGH: hosting is sticky (RSS migration friction) plus unlimited-shows lock-in; churn discussed openly on Build Your SaaS (5% figure used in planning post).
legalPrivacy: Standard SaaS: owns no creator content (terms); podcast analytics privacy per policy; no extraordinary legal burden evidenced.
acquisitionDifficulty: MEDIUM: crowded SEO and entrenched free hosts; founder audience was the unfair advantage, not replicable cheaply.
monetizationDifficulty: LOW: clear $19-$199 subscription value metric (downloads/private subs); trial-to-paid engine established.
zeroUpfront: POSSIBLY: code-first SaaS with modest hosting costs; founders self-funded and kept day jobs until $20k MRR, so near-zero but not literally zero.
mrr100: HIGH: $19-$99/mo self-serve with unlimited-shows wedge; reached team-sustaining MRR within ~1 year; solo founder could reach $100 MRR with a handful of customers.
learn: Audience-first bootstrapping works: pre-built trust converts to first revenue; building in public compounds into distribution; saying no to oversized customers protects focus.
notCopy: Do not copy the crowded general-hosting wedge directly; Transistor won via founder audience + support reputation, both slow to replicate; incumbents now bundle video/AI.
